name: gameplay-birthday-push
origin: A toy hand pushing the player (checkpoint 5, feature motion), on the round of gameplay-birthday-start (seed 11, Arcade, Normal, robot 0, BirthdayPartyStage2; the AI robots stopped at the round's first frame): the reposition fixture puts the player on (12,7), in front of the right-facing hand on (11,7), with a box on (13,7). ToyHand.runEngine opens every hand at tick 105 (hand-open) and on the hand clip's pushComplete frame sets the robot's hitHand; PushRobotCommand.moveFuc snaps it back from the box cell (first-push, as in docs/evidence/edition-5-interactions.md). The hand opens again at tick 538; this push keeps the stale checked cell, so the player moves 15 px per tick (push-mid) into the box cell (push-end) and stays there once the hand is closed (closed).
godot_note: Godot's player is put on the same cell (Game.reposition_human); the robot's display follows the simulation's push (scripts/ui/game_actors.gd).

actions.godot_note: The round this START opens takes its board and enemy robots from the golden of the birthday-start capture (App.round_as_recorded), as gameplay-cinema-start does.
AIControl.stop through the original's own method (fixture); Godot gives the robot no commands, as it then has none.
